# Happier — Testing Infrastructure Audit Tracker

- **Working status (2026-02-28)**: We are actively iterating on UI performance + SCM review UX (virtualized review rendering, details-pane scroll/focus mode, agent-input popovers). Keep this section up to date to avoid re-validating already-fixed items after context compaction.
  - **Recently fixed (validated by UI unit tests / UI e2e)**:
    - Review collapse/expand state not reflecting for visible rows (FlashList `extraData` + collapsed state baked into `data`).
    - Review virtualization stability (FlashList + `getItemType` + large-diff auto-collapse to keep rendering bounded and avoid scroll gaps).
    - Review focus-path UX on web (focus scroll is non-animated; avoids scroll/event edge cases).
    - Review large-diff performance/scroll stability:
      - diffs auto-collapse outside the current viewability window when the review exceeds thresholds (reduces DOM height + prevents large blank gaps)
      - viewability index updates are sorted/deduped and committed only when changed (prevents redundant rerenders + feedback loops)
    - Review expand/collapse stability on FlashList v2: we clear FlashList layout cache before toggling a row, preventing long-lived blank gaps after dynamic height changes (diff blocks, image previews).
    - Review scroll persistence correctness on web:
      - `onScrollTopChange` now finds the real scroll container (descendants *or ancestors*), preventing `scrollTop` from being persisted as `0` for virtualized lists
      - expand/collapse scroll correction is applied against the correct scroll root (overflow-aware), making the “collapse without jump” behavior deterministic
      - cross-session Review restore no longer targets the wrong DOM node: the web scroll-root is resolved from the FlashList ref and cached per mounted instance (no global `document.querySelector` fallbacks that can hit a hidden session/tab)
      - collapsed-path state now persists on every toggle (deduped + sorted), so cross-session switching restores the exact expanded/collapsed diffs reliably
    - Details-pane tab state robustness:
      - scroll snapshots are de-duped by `data-testid` (largest-overflow wins) to avoid restoring the wrong nested scrollable when multiple nodes resolve to the same stable id
      - file editor draft persistence no longer creates a maximum-update-depth loop (draft persistence callbacks depend on stable pane methods, not the pane object identity)
      - when a persisted draft indicates the user was editing, the file-details tab stays in `file` mode on re-mount/session switch so the unsaved textarea/draft is preserved
      - pinned-tab UI now has a distinct pinned indicator vs the preview “pin” action (prevents ambiguous “pin looks the same” UX)
    - Link-file action regression + UX polish:
      - chip click opens *and* toggles closed correctly
      - avoids immediate re-open when Popover closes itself in pointerdown-capture ordering
      - matches full composer width when anchored to the agent-input overlay anchor
      - portal popovers now stay hidden until content layout is known for **top/bottom** placements (prevents visible “jump”/flicker on open)
    - Files sidebar progressive refresh:
      - repository tree root reload keeps the previous tree visible (stale-while-revalidate) instead of blanking the list
      - shows an inline loading/error row at the top while revalidating
      - repository directory entries now seed from an in-memory cache on mount/session-switch, so reopening the Files sidebar can render immediately while the root revalidates
      - session view now warms the repository root directory cache (web) in the background so first open is more likely to render immediately
    - SCM/files derived-data hot path optimizations:
      - SCM right-sidebar commit tab now skips session attribution work when rendering repository-only changed-file lists (`useChangedFilesData({ computeAttribution: false })`), reducing open-tab jank on large repos.
      - `snapshotToScmStatusFiles(...)` now memoizes per snapshot instance to avoid recomputing the same file lists in multiple UI surfaces
      - repository tree SCM badge index now memoizes per snapshot instance and is computed after first paint on web (progressive badge hydration; file tree renders first)
    - Review “open file” actions on web now defer pane mutations via `deferOnWeb(...)`, preventing react-native-web PressResponder crashes (e.g. `nativeEvent` restore-state errors) when opening a file from review.
    - Focus-mode sidebar hiding on web/tablet: when editor focus mode is enabled, the permanent drawer switches to a hidden front-drawer mode so it does not reserve layout space.
    - Session right/details panes show a visible loading fallback while the pane modules are lazy-loaded (avoids “blank pane” during slow first-load).
    - Multi-pane overlayStack UX: when the right pane is logically open but hidden behind an overlay details pane, it stays mounted so closing details reveals the sidebar instantly (no remount/fetch).
    - SCM panel performance: commit history fetch is now lazy (loads only when the History subtab is opened), reducing commit-tab lag/jank from background log resets.
    - `createAdvancedDebounce`/`createCustomDebounce`: `delay <= 0` now executes immediately (no timers), eliminating test warnings and reducing overhead for “disabled debounce” configs.
    - Pierre diff viewer: multi-file patch extraction now handles leading-slash `filePath` values so the correct file diff is selected (prevents mis-rendering when SCM paths are absolute-ish like `/src/foo.ts`).
    - SessionView cleanup: removed an unused `editorFocusModeEnabled` subscription in `SessionViewLoaded` (focus mode is handled by `AppPaneScopeHost`).
    - File-path presentation unification:
      - SCM changed-file rows now normalize leading slashes in `fileName` and render `dir/` on the left with `filename` on the right (root files still align filename to the right column)
      - Files search results now match this layout (path-left, filename-right) so file lists look consistent across Files/SCM/@ suggestions
    - UI e2e coverage added for SCM review state retention:
      - `packages/tests/suites/ui-e2e/session.sourceControl.reviewScroll.spec.ts` covers Review scroll, collapse persistence, per-session right pane open/close retention, tab switching scroll retention, link-file popover toggle, unsaved editor draft retention, and cross-session restoration.
      - `packages/tests/suites/ui-e2e/session.sourceControl.partialStaging.spec.ts` covers patch-based staging (selected lines), mixed commit selection (whole-file + patch), commit persistence of remaining changes, discard confirmation flow, and opening the latest History commit diff.
  - **Still in progress / needs UI validation**:
    - Ensure remaining scrollable details-pane content surfaces have consistent scroll affordances (edge fades + indicators) where appropriate.

- [x] Duplicate testing of `@happier-dev/agents` helpers inside app-level suites — **Observed:** CLI unit tests re-assert workspace-helper semantics that appear to belong to `packages/agents` (e.g. `apps/cli/src/agent/runtime/sessionControlsPublishShared.test.ts`, `apps/cli/src/agent/runtime/permissionModeForAgent.test.ts`, `apps/cli/src/agent/runtime/monotonicUpdatedAt.test.ts`). **Impact:** cross-suite drift risk (two suites must be kept in sync), and app tests become noisy/less focused on app behavior. **Next:** keep canonical helper tests in `packages/agents`; in app suites, prefer (a) small smoke “wiring uses helper” tests or (b) integration tests that validate the app behavior end-to-end without re-testing helper internals.
- [x] Duplicated “temp git repo fixture” harnesses in script/unit tests — **Observed:** `apps/stack/scripts/utils/git/{default_branch,dev_checkout,fast_forward_to_remote}.test.mjs` each re-implements bare repo init + clone + commit + branch/remote wiring; SwiftBar git cache tests also seed repos ad hoc. **Impact:** duplicated git setup is verbose and easy to drift (missing config, branch defaults, cleanup semantics), and increases flake risk in CI with parallel runs. **Next:** extract one small `withTempGitFixture(t, { bare?, branches?, remotes? })` helper (node:test-compatible) and standardize git user config + cleanup + command runner.
- [x] Duplicated “prepend PATH with stub binaries” pattern (fake `yarn`/`expo`/`gh`/`osascript`/`codex`/etc.) — **Observed:** multiple `apps/stack/scripts/**/*.test.mjs` (e.g. `command_workspace_deps_built.test.mjs`, `swiftbar_wt_pr_backcompat.test.mjs`, `utils/llm/tools.test.mjs`) write executable scripts into a temp `bin/` and patch `process.env.PATH`. **Impact:** repeated boilerplate + inconsistent restore/cleanup; windows/PATH-separator edge cases are easy to miss. **Next:** standardize a `withTempPathBin(t, { commands: {name: script} })` helper that handles chmod + platform separators + env restore.
- [x] Duplicated “localhost server + reserved port” harnesses for Expo/Metro probing — **Observed:** `apps/stack/scripts/utils/expo/{expo_state_running,metro_ports}.test.mjs` and several `expo_dev_*` tests each implement their own port reservation + `/status` responder servers. **Impact:** drift risk (slightly different status strings/timeouts) and flake risk (port binding + close timing) scattered across files. **Next:** centralize `reservePort()` + `withStatusServer({ text })` helpers and keep per-test assertions focused on behavior.
- [x] Duplicated “poll until condition” test loops (files/pids/ps sampling) — **Observed:** `apps/stack/scripts/utils/proc/{ownership_killProcessGroupOwnedByStack,ownership_listPidsWithEnvNeedles,terminate}.test.mjs` each hand-roll polling loops (`waitForCondition`, `waitForFile`, `waitForPidExit`) with slightly different timeouts/intervals; similar polling exists in Expo verbose-log and other process tests. **Impact:** inconsistent timeout semantics and increased flake risk under slow CI; hard to tune globally. **Next:** standardize on a single `waitFor({ predicate, timeoutMs, intervalMs, description })` helper per runner (node:test + Vitest), and reuse across suites.
- [x] Repeated “backend wrapper argv/wiring” tests across agent backends (Claude/Auggie/etc.) — **Observed:** tests that cast into internal backend options and assert raw argv/rule strings (e.g. `apps/cli/src/backends/auggie/acp/backend.permissions.test.ts`, `apps/cli/src/backends/claude/claudeLocal.test.ts`, plus CLI command wiring tests). **Impact:** high churn risk on refactors that preserve behavior but change args composition; increases patchwork feel across suites. **Next:** extract a shared “backend launch plan” adapter that returns a structured plan (`{ executable, args, env }`) and test that, keeping only a small number of smoke tests that assert the wrapper calls the plan.
- [x] Repeated ad-hoc “temp dir + write fixture files + exec node script” harnesses — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/tools/tauri/make-latest-json.test.ts` and other tooling/scan tests using custom tmpdir + fs helpers. **Impact:** duplicated cleanup patterns and slightly divergent helpers increase leak/flake risk (tmp dirs not removed on crash) and make infra tests harder to read. **Next:** extract a small shared `withTempDir` + `writeFile` test helper (per suite) and prefer promise-based APIs where possible; keep these infra tests in a dedicated tooling lane if they grow.
- [x] Duplicated Vitest lane config boilerplate across `packages/tests` suites — **Observed:** `packages/tests/vitest.core*.config.ts`, `packages/tests/vitest.providers.config.ts`, `packages/tests/vitest.stress.config.ts` repeat the same `environment:'node'`, long timeouts, `globals:false`, `env:{HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV:''}`, and `exclude:[...resolveVitestFeatureTestExcludeGlobs()]` patterns with only minor include/exclude differences. **Impact:** drift risk (feature gating / defaults can diverge silently) and makes “is this test wired?” harder to reason about. **Next:** extract a small shared `defineHappierVitestConfig({ include, excludeExtra, timeouts, pool, fileParallelism })` helper so each lane declares only what’s unique.
- [x] Repeated `process.env` save/restore boilerplate in tests — **Observed:** multiple provider-contract e2e-ish tests manually snapshot a list of env vars, mutate them, and restore in `finally` (e.g. `packages/tests/suites/providers/harness.inFlightSteer.*.e2e.test.ts`, `packages/tests/suites/providers/harness.tokenTelemetry.acpStub.e2e.test.ts`), plus similar patterns across other suites. **Impact:** easy to miss variables (leaks between tests), verbose setup obscures intent, and makes it harder to safely add new env-gated behavior. **Next:** standardize on a tiny helper like `withEnvOverrides({ KEY:'1' }, fn)` (supports delete/restore) and encourage per-suite “known env var set” constants.
- [x] Repeated provider-spec loading + traversal boilerplate — **Observed:** many `packages/tests/suites/providers/providerSpecs.*.test.ts` files call `loadProvidersFromCliSpecs()` per test and re-implement `providers.find(...)` + tier extraction and long `not.toContain(...)` exclusion lists. **Impact:** slower suite + brittle churn when scenario catalogs or provider policies change; logic is duplicated rather than table-driven. **Next:** add a tiny “load once” helper + shared assertion utilities (e.g. `expectProviderScenariosExcluded(providerId, tier, ids[])`) and keep per-provider policy in one table.
- [x] Inline “fake ACP JSON-RPC agent script” + subprocess harness duplication — **Observed:** repeated across many `apps/cli/src/agent/acp/**/__tests__/*.test.ts` files (e.g. `AcpBackend.authenticate.test.ts`, `AcpBackend.configOptions.test.ts`, `AcpBackend.sessionModes.test.ts`, `AcpBackend.sessionModels.test.ts`, `AcpBackend.waitForResponseComplete.test.ts`, `AcpBackend.toolCallUpdate.*.test.ts`, `AcpBackend.permissionSeed.*.test.ts`). **Impact:** copy/pasted JSON parsing + tempdir lifecycle + polling/timeouts increases drift and flake risk; makes it harder to add new provider-compat cases consistently; can inflate unit-lane runtime. **Next:** extract a shared ACP testkit/harness (single place for spawn + cleanup + default timeouts + wait helpers) and parameterize fake agent behavior (prompt → updates, permission request flows, stderr/stdout injection, exit/signal behaviors).
- [x] Repeated “export exists” smoke tests via `(module as unknown as { fn?: unknown }).fn` — **Observed:** `packages/protocol/src/bugReports.fallback.test.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/bugReports.reporter.test.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/sync/http/client.runtimeFetch.test.ts` (similar “method exists” check). **Impact:** these tests mostly validate export presence/typing rather than behavior; they’re brittle to refactors (rename/re-export) and can mask dead code (export exists but behavior wrong). **Next:** replace with direct imports + behavior assertions where possible; if the goal is “public API surface must include X”, consolidate into a single table-driven “exports surface” test per package (or rely on TS + exports map tests) instead of scattering one-off existence checks.
- [x] Call-forwarding/wiring tests with huge dependency mocks — **Observed:** protocol action executor tests with `createDeps()` (`packages/protocol/src/actions/actionExecutor.*.test.ts`) and many UI unit tests that mock deep internal modules to verify a screen calls a hook/handler with specific props (`apps/ui/sources/__tests__/app/**`). **Impact:** high maintenance, low signal (tests wiring + identity instead of outcomes), and encourages “patchwork” mocking patterns. **Next:** (1) extract a shared typed `ActionExecutorDeps` test builder (or table-driven matrices) to cut duplication; (2) for UI, prefer testing pure request-builders/state reducers directly and keep screen tests focused on user-observable outcomes (navigation/events) with minimal internal mocks; (3) consider moving orchestration-heavy/wiring-with-mocks tests to a distinct lane if they remain.
- [x] Repeated global `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` toggles + no unified cleanup — **Observed:** many UI unit/integration tests set `globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true` (sometimes via helpers like `enableReactActEnvironment()`) without a consistent restore/reset strategy, alongside repeated `react-test-renderer` + `act` scaffolding. **Impact:** increases cross-test coupling/leak risk (especially with `vi.resetModules()` usage) and makes the “fast lane” harder to reason about. **Next:** standardize via one Vitest setup helper that (a) sets it once per worker, (b) documents why, and (c) ensures global state cleanup remains deterministic (pair with `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` / `vi.restoreAllMocks()` and explicit module resets only where needed).
- [x] Repeated “mock storage.getState via vi.mock + mutable state object” harnesses — **Observed:** many UI unit specs (notably voice) rely on `vi.mock('@/sync/domains/state/storage', () => ({ storage: { getState: () => state } }))` plus manual resets/mutation (e.g. `apps/ui/sources/voice/agent/VoiceAgentSessionController.*.spec.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/voice/adapters/*.spec.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/voice/agent/teleportVoiceAgentToSessionRoot.test.ts`). **Impact:** brittle coupling to store shape, encourages internal mocking over real behavior, and increases drift risk (tests manually maintain large partial state objects). **Next:** prefer using the real `storage` store with `storage.setState` seed helpers (pattern already used in `apps/ui/sources/voice/context/voiceHooks.privacy.spec.ts`) and/or extract a typed `seedStorageState()` helper per suite to standardize resets and reduce patchwork.
- [x] Repeated ad-hoc “microtask polling” loops for async waits — **Observed:** multiple voice/local engine specs wait for side effects with `for (...) await Promise.resolve()` loops (e.g. `apps/ui/sources/voice/local/localVoiceEngine.agent.spec.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/voice/local/localVoiceEngine.tts.spec.ts`). **Impact:** unpredictable runtime under load and higher flake risk; tests can become “slow/patchwork” as more waits are added. **Next:** standardize on a small `waitFor(condition, { timeoutMs, tick })` helper (or event-driven harness hooks) so waits are bounded, readable, and consistent across the suite.
- [x] Near-identical “dynamic probe cache” implementations (models vs session modes) — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/sync/domains/models/dynamicModelProbeCache.ts` and `apps/ui/sources/sync/domains/sessionModes/dynamicSessionModeProbeCache.ts` share ~the same persistence/hydration/pruning/dedupe logic (only value shape + key/id strings differ). **Impact:** fixes/features (TTL rules, persistence limits, corruption handling) must be duplicated; drift risk is high and tests must cover both. **Next:** extract a generic `createDynamicProbeCache<T>({ persistKey, storageId, normalize, cacheErrorMessage })` or unify into one module with typed adapters; keep thin wrappers per domain.
- [x] Repeated “constrained content width” (pins `layout.maxWidth` container styles) across UI screens — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/app/(app)/runs.test.tsx`, `apps/ui/sources/app/(app)/session/[id]/runs.test.tsx`, `apps/ui/sources/app/(app)/session/[id]/runs/[runId].test.tsx`, `apps/ui/sources/app/(app)/session/[id]/runs/new.test.tsx`, `apps/ui/sources/app/(app)/session/[id]/files.test.tsx` (and more). **Impact:** low behavior signal (asserts layout implementation detail) + churn risk if layout implementation changes (style refactor, container component swap). **Next:** either (a) centralize as 1–2 smoke tests for “screens use SharedConstrainedContainer” or (b) assert via a shared “constrained container” component presence, not raw style shape; avoid repeating per-screen style pins unless a specific regression occurred.
- [x] Repeated react-test-renderer traversal + “flush effects” helpers — **Observed:** many UI screen/component tests define local `flushRender()` (`await Promise.resolve()` loops / `setTimeout(0)`) and local `findPressableByText`/`findPressableByLabel` tree-walkers (e.g. `apps/ui/sources/components/automations/screens/*.test.tsx`, plus multiple `apps/ui/sources/__tests__/app/**`). **Impact:** duplicated + slightly divergent helpers increase brittleness and make tests hard to read; tree-walking via parent links is sensitive to refactors. **Next:** extract a single small UI testkit (react-test-renderer utilities + stable finders) and prefer asserting on stable accessibility labels/testIDs rather than copy when possible.
- [x] Repeated “daemon unavailable” alert + Retry + unmount-safe retry tests — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/hooks/ui/useHappyAction.daemonUnavailable.test.tsx`, `apps/ui/sources/hooks/session/files/executeScmCommit.daemonUnavailable.test.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/hooks/session/files/useFileScmStageActions.daemonUnavailable.test.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/hooks/session/files/useFilesScmOperations.daemonUnavailable.test.ts`, plus earlier session/editor/spawn daemon-unavailable specs. **Impact:** duplicated “find Retry button by text key + press after unmount does not retry” scaffolding and multiple ad-hoc classifications can drift. **Next:** centralize (1) RPC/SCM error→daemon-unavailable classification, (2) a single `showDaemonUnavailableAlert({ detail, onRetry, shouldContinue })` helper, and (3) a table-driven test matrix to cover classification + mount-safety once.
- [x] Perf-heavy “large payload” fixtures in unit lanes — **Observed:** UI unit tests generating multi-megabyte strings / tens-of-thousands-of-lines text to exercise chunking or “no negative stats” edges (e.g. `apps/ui/sources/components/ui/code/editor/bridge/chunkedBridge.test.ts` uses ~2.5MB strings; `apps/ui/sources/components/ui/code/model/diff/diffViewModel.test.ts` builds 15k/16k-line texts). **Impact:** slows the fast lane, increases memory/GC pressure, and can introduce time-sensitive flake under load. **Next:** centralize reusable big fixtures (generated once), shrink payload sizes while still crossing thresholds (lower `maxChunkBytes` / targeted stat clamp unit tests), and consider a dedicated perf/regression lane for “big input” tests if they remain necessary.
- [x] Multi-megabyte base64 roundtrip tests in fast lane — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/encryption/base64.test.ts` allocates 5,000,000 bytes (base64) and 3,000,000 bytes (base64url) and validates via checksum. **Impact:** very expensive CPU/memory in unit lane; risks timeouts on busy CI runners. **Next:** reduce payload sizes while still exercising “large payload” code paths (or move to a perf/regression lane), and reuse a shared deterministic-bytes fixture generator across crypto tests.
- [x] Duplicated web safety checks for “raw string under `<View>`” + disabled cursor policy — **Observed:** multiple list/menu tests assert that primitive string children (e.g. `"."`) are wrapped under `Text` (not rendered as raw string children of a `View`) in both `apps/ui/sources/components/ui/lists/ActionListSection.test.tsx` and `apps/ui/sources/components/ui/lists/Item.subtitleNormalization.test.tsx`; disabled cursor (`cursor:'not-allowed'`) is asserted in both `apps/ui/sources/components/ui/lists/SelectableRow.cursor.spec.tsx` and `apps/ui/sources/components/ui/lists/Item.subtitleNormalization.test.tsx`. **Impact:** duplicated tree-walk/style-resolution assertions and patchwork UX contracts scattered across components. **Next:** extract shared helpers for (a) “web-safe text children” normalization and (b) disabled cursor style policy, test them once, and keep only minimal per-component smoke tests.
- [x] Tool renderer tests duplicate “truncation/list summary” contracts + copy pinning — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/components/tools/renderers/fileOps/{GlobView,LSView,GrepView,DeleteView,CodeSearchView,WebSearchView}.test.tsx` and `apps/ui/sources/components/tools/renderers/{system/BashView,workflow/ReasoningView,web/WebFetchView}.test.tsx` repeatedly assert `+N more`/ellipsis truncation and detailLevel expansion using host-text concatenation alongside repeated `ToolSectionView` passthrough mocks. **Impact:** duplication + churn risk (changing thresholds/copy requires editing many files) and tests skew toward formatting rather than stable semantics. **Next:** centralize truncation/list-summary behavior in a shared component/hook with one table-driven contract test; keep only a small number of per-view smoke tests for unique formatting.
- [x] Tool timeline row tests share massive “mock the world” scaffolding — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/components/tools/shell/views/ToolTimelineRow.*.test.tsx` (e.g. `minimalFallback`, `tapAction`, plus upcoming `unknownCollapse`, `titleFallback`) each mock RN primitives/Animated, unistyles theme, router, catalog/registry, normalization/inference, error parsing, Text wrappers, and settings state to assert one small conditional behavior. **Impact:** high maintenance + patchwork risk; tests are mostly validating mocked composition rather than real user-observable outcomes; makes it easy for mocks to drift and hide regressions. **Next:** extract pure policy helpers for (a) tap action resolution, (b) expand/collapse defaults, (c) minimal/unknown tool rendering rules, and add a shared harness for the few integration assertions that still matter (navigation + stable testIDs).
- [x] Repeated “AgentInput” mega-mock boilerplate across many small UI tests — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/components/sessions/agentInput/AgentInput.*.test.tsx` repeatedly mock `react-native` (via `reactNativeStub`), storage settings, agent catalog, model/perms helpers, autocomplete hooks, and many UI shell components to assert a single small UI contract (icons/testIDs/accessibility). **Impact:** high maintenance + patchwork risk (small changes to AgentInput wiring force edits across many files); also makes it easy to accidentally test stubbed behavior rather than real UI logic. **Next:** create a shared AgentInput test harness (central mocks + minimal knobs) and prefer moving pure logic to helper modules with pure tests (keep only a small number of high-signal component tests for testIDs/a11y/interaction contracts).
- [x] Repeated deterministic RNG helpers in crypto tests — **Observed:** `deterministicRandomBytesFactory()` duplicated in `packages/protocol/src/crypto/accountScopedCipher.test.ts`, `boxBundle.test.ts`, `encryptedDataKeyEnvelopeV1.test.ts`, `terminalProvisioningV2.test.ts`. **Impact:** trivial duplication but repeated “randomBytes override” plumbing hides what each test actually cares about and invites slight divergence. **Next:** introduce a single shared `testDeterministicRandomBytes()` helper (or a `makeDeterministicRandomBytes(seed?)`) local to crypto tests; keep per-test overrides explicit (don’t broaden to production code).
- [x] Repeated “pin exported string constants” tests — **Observed:** `packages/protocol/src/rpc.*.test.ts` assert exact method string ids (`RPC_METHODS`, `SESSION_RPC_METHODS`) and similar constant pinning appears elsewhere. **Impact:** can be high-signal when these strings are wire contracts, but duplication across many files creates churn/patchwork (every new method requires updating multiple tests). **Next:** consolidate into 1–2 table-driven contract tests per surface (daemon vs session) that validate uniqueness + expected prefixes + a curated list of “must not change” ids; avoid scattering constant pins per topic unless there’s a compatibility reason.

- [x] Repeated “dynamic preflight probe” tests across models and session modes — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/components/sessions/new/hooks/screenModel/useNewSessionPreflightModelsState.{cache,cwd,persistence,refresh}.test.tsx` and `apps/ui/sources/components/sessions/new/hooks/screenModel/useNewSessionPreflightSessionModesState.{cache,cwd,loadingPlaceholder,persistence,refresh}.test.tsx` share near-identical harnesses (reset cache, mount hook, flush `setTimeout(0)`, assert request shape/options/caching). **Impact:** patchwork + churn risk (timeout/id changes require editing many files; persistence semantics tested via module reload are easy to flake). **Next:** consolidate into one table-driven probe test suite per probe type (models vs modes) using a shared helper for mount/flush/reset, and consider whether “persistence across app restart” belongs in a slower lane or can be validated with a smaller unit around the persistence adapter.

- [x] Repeated `ScmWorkingSnapshot`/SCM snapshot fixtures across UI SCM tests — **Observed:** many SCM unit tests inline large `ScmWorkingSnapshot`/protocol snapshot objects (`apps/ui/sources/scm/scmRepositoryService.test.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/scm/scmStatusFiles.test.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/scm/registry/scmUiBackendRegistry.test.ts`, etc.). **Impact:** drift risk when SCM snapshot shape/capabilities evolve (tests pin large objects), and duplicates “canonical snapshot” construction logic. **Next:** extract a typed `makeScmWorkingSnapshot(overrides)` + `makeProtocolScmSnapshot(overrides)` in a single SCM testkit file (or `satisfies` builders) and have tests assert only relevant subsets.
- [x] Repeated “API client test harness” patterns (server snapshot + immediate backoff + fetch stub) — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/sync/api/account/apiConnectedServicesQuotasV2.test.ts` and `apps/ui/sources/sync/api/account/apiConnectedServicesV2.test.ts` both `doMock` `getActiveServerSnapshot`, mock `backoff/backoffForever` to immediate, and stub `globalThis.fetch`, plus repeat credentials fixtures + module reset in `afterEach`. **Impact:** duplicated harness logic and cleanup increases flake risk (module cache/global leaks) and slows iteration when adding more API client tests. **Next:** introduce a shared Vitest helper (e.g. `installApiClientTestHarness({ serverUrl })`) that sets server snapshot, stubs backoff, installs/restores fetch, and provides a typed `jsonFetchResponse(...)`.
- [x] Repeated “settings defaults policing” across settings-domain tests — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/sync/domains/settings/settings.spec.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/sync/domains/settings/settings.providerPlugins.test.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/sync/domains/settings/localSettings.test.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/sync/domains/settings/voiceSettings.spec.ts` all pin large surfaces of default values (some duplicated across files). **Impact:** churny/brittle tests that block harmless UX/config tuning; encourages patchwork (adding new default assertions in “whatever file touched”) and increases unit-lane runtime. **Next:** consolidate default assertions into 1–2 high-signal “defaults shape + invariants” tests, and keep the rest focused on migrations/validation/compat (table-driven where possible). Treat exact IDs/assets/voice ids as contract only when truly required.
- [x] Repeated “trailing JSON after preamble” parsers + near-identical tests across execution-run profiles — **Observed:** `apps/cli/src/agent/executionRuns/profiles/delegate/DelegateProfile.test.ts`, `apps/cli/src/agent/executionRuns/profiles/plan/PlanProfile.test.ts`, `apps/cli/src/agent/executionRuns/profiles/review/ReviewProfile.test.ts` all re-test “model output may have preamble text; parse trailing strict JSON; fail deterministically on non-JSON” with highly similar `start` fixtures. **Impact:** duplicated coverage increases maintenance and encourages drift (small behavior changes require edits in multiple files). **Next:** extract a shared `parseTrailingStrictJson()` helper + a table-driven shared test that all profiles can reuse, and keep per-profile tests focused on schema-specific fields (e.g., plan sections, review CodeRabbit parsing, delegate deliverables).
- [x] Divergent MMKV stubbing strategies (global vs per-file) — **Observed:** global mocks in `apps/ui/sources/dev/vitestSetup.ts` alongside per-file `vi.mock('react-native-mmkv', ...)` in `apps/ui/sources/sync/domains/state/persistence.test.ts` (and other storage tests). **Impact:** inconsistent stub behavior + cleanup patterns can mask bugs or cause subtle cross-test drift/leaks. **Next:** standardize on a single MMKV test adapter/harness (shared in UI testkit) and ensure tests either (a) use injected storage instances or (b) use a consistent global mock with explicit reset hooks.
- [x] Push token registration tests + harness duplicated across syncAccount engine tests — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/sync/engine/account/syncAccount.pushTokenLogging.test.ts` and `apps/ui/sources/sync/engine/account/syncAccount.pushTokenMultiServer.test.ts` both set up similar mocks for Expo notifications/constants/platform, stub network, and assert “never log raw push token”. **Impact:** duplicated setup + overlapping intent makes changes to registration behavior/log wording expensive and increases risk of inconsistent coverage/cleanup. **Next:** extract a shared `arrangePushTokenRegistrationHarness({ profiles, active, failures })` helper and keep one integration-style “multi-server request fanout” test plus a small number of pure-unit tests for selection/fallback/log redaction.
- [x] Near-identical “key becomes available later” encryption lifecycle tests — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/sync/encryption/encryption.initializeMachines.keyUpdate.test.ts` and `apps/ui/sources/sync/encryption/encryption.initializeSessions.keyUpdate.test.ts`. **Impact:** duplication encourages drift when encryption lifecycle semantics change. **Next:** table-drive the shared behavior with a parameter (`initializeMachines` vs `initializeSessions`, getter name) and keep per-surface tests minimal.
- [x] Repeated socket update “base params” harness + broad dependency injection — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/sync/engine/socket/socket.automationUpdates.test.ts`, `socket.cursorIsolation.test.ts`, `socket.newMachineUpdates.test.ts` each re-creates a large `buildBaseParams(...)` object for `handleUpdateContainer`. **Impact:** patchwork harness drift risk and low-signal wiring assertions (many injected fns never used by a given test). **Next:** extract a single typed `createSocketUpdateHarness({ overrides })` helper that centralizes defaults + cleanup, and keep tests focused on specific invalidations/state changes.
- [x] Repeated “server-scoped routing” tests (active socket vs scoped runtimeFetch/ephemeral) — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/sync/ops/__tests__/sessionArchive.serverScope.test.ts`, `sessionDelete.serverScope.test.ts`, `sessionStop.serverScope.test.ts`, plus many server-scoped machine/session ops routing tests (`apps/ui/sources/sync/ops/machineExecutionRuns.test.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/sync/ops/machines.*.test.ts`, `apps/ui/sources/sync/ops/sessions.serverScoped.test.ts`). **Impact:** lots of call-forwarding assertions + repeated `resolveServerScoped*Context`/`makeResponse` boilerplate; higher drift risk when server-scoped transport changes. **Next:** (1) extract a single typed “serverScoped op harness” for unit tests (context resolver stub + active vs scoped request executor), (2) table-drive endpoint/method matrices, (3) keep a small number of behavior-level tests asserting fallback semantics (METHOD_NOT_AVAILABLE → event fallback) instead of repeating call shapes everywhere.
- [x] Overlapping reducer/AgentState permission scenario tests spread across multiple files — **Observed:** `apps/ui/sources/sync/reducer/reducer.spec.ts` (very large matrix), `apps/ui/sources/sync/reducer/phase0-skipping.spec.ts`, and smaller focused tests like `apps/ui/sources/sync/reducer/permissionPlaceholder.toolResultOverride.test.ts` and `apps/ui/sources/sync/reducer/helpers/thinkingText.test.ts`. **Impact:** duplicated scenarios + repeated inline fixtures makes refactors risky, increases runtime/maintenance, and creates “patchwork” coverage (same intent asserted in different places with slightly different expectations). **Next:** split the monolith into focused files per concern (localId dedupe, streaming merge, tool lifecycle, permission matching), extract typed fixture builders (`makeNormalizedMessage`, `makeAgentStateRequest`, `makeToolCall`, `makeToolResult`), and keep only a small number of end-to-end race scenario tests.

## Global entrypoints

- `yarn test` → `yarn -s test:unit`
- `yarn test:db-contract:docker` → `yarn -s test:db-contract:postgres:docker && yarn -s test:db-contract:mysql:docker`

- `apps/ui/package.json` (name=`@happier-dev/app`)

  - `test`: `$npm_execpath run test:unit`

  - `test:unit`: `$npm_execpath run build && vitest run --config vitest.config.ts`
- `apps/server/package.json` (name=`@happier-dev/server`)
  - `test`: `yarn -s test:unit`
  - `test:db-contract`: `vitest run --isolate -c vitest.dbcontract.config.ts`
  - `test:integration`: `vitest run --isolate -c vitest.integration.config.ts`
  - `test:server:db-contract`: `yarn -s test:db-contract`
  - `test:unit`: `vitest run --isolate -c vitest.config.ts`
- `apps/stack/package.json` (name=`@happier-dev/stack`)
  - `test`: `yarn -s test:unit`
  - `test:ci`: `yarn -s test:unit`
  - `test:integration`: `node ./scripts/test_integration.mjs`
  - `test:unit`: `node ./scripts/test_ci.mjs`
- `packages/protocol/package.json` (name=`@happier-dev/protocol`)
  - `test`: `vitest run`
- `packages/agents/package.json` (name=`@happier-dev/agents`)
  - `test`: `vitest run --config ../../vitest.config.ts`
- `packages/tests/package.json` (name=`@happier-dev/tests`)
  - `test`: `node scripts/run-vitest-with-heartbeat.mjs --config vitest.core.config.ts`
  - `test:core:fast`: `node scripts/run-vitest-with-heartbeat.mjs --config vitest.core.fast.config.ts`
  - `test:core:slow`: `node scripts/run-vitest-with-heartbeat.mjs --config vitest.core.slow.config.ts`
  - `test:providers`: `node scripts/run-vitest-with-heartbeat.mjs --config vitest.providers.config.ts`
  - `test:stress`: `node scripts/run-vitest-with-heartbeat.mjs --config vitest.stress.config.ts`
  - `test:ui:e2e`: `playwright test -c playwright.ui.config.mjs`
- `packages/relay-server/package.json` (name=`@happier-dev/relay-server`)
  - `test`: `HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV= node --test`
- `packages/cli-common/package.json` (name=`@happier-dev/cli-common`)
  - `test`: `yarn -s build && HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV= node --test "tests/*.test.mjs"`
- `packages/release-runtime/package.json` (name=`@happier-dev/release-runtime`)
  - `test`: `yarn -s build && HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV= node --test "tests/*.test.mjs"`

## Shared gating & infrastructure

- Feature-gated tests by filename marker: `**/*.feat.<featureId>.*`
- Feature gating env vars (global): `HAPPIER_BUILD_FEATURES_ALLOW`, `HAPPIER_BUILD_FEATURES_DENY`, `HAPPIER_TEST_FEATURES_DENY`, plus embedded `HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV` / `HAPPIER_EMBEDDED_POLICY_ENV`
- Gating implementation: `scripts/testing/featureTestGating.ts`
- E2E DB selection env vars (packages/tests): `HAPPIER_E2E_DB_PROVIDER` / `HAPPY_E2E_DB_PROVIDER`, and `DATABASE_URL` for postgres/mysql
- Inventory excludes generated dirs by name: `output/`, `test-results/`, `playwright-report/`, `coverage/`, `.project/`, `dist/`, `node_modules/`

## Shared infra reviews (completed)

- [x] `scripts/testing/featureTestGating.ts` — **What it covers:** shared feature-test gating: resolves disabled feature ids via embedded env (`HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV`/`HAPPIER_EMBEDDED_POLICY_ENV`) + allow/deny (`HAPPIER_BUILD_FEATURES_ALLOW`, `HAPPIER_BUILD_FEATURES_DENY`, `HAPPIER_TEST_FEATURES_DENY`), applies dependency closure over `FEATURE_CATALOG`, and returns Vitest exclude globs `**/*.feat.<featureId>.*`. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real protocol feature catalog/policy evaluation; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium (relies on feature ids/deps; deny env can silently skip tests if not surfaced). **Speed/flakiness risks:** none (pure). **Duplication candidates:** keep all “deny list” derivation centralized here (avoid ad-hoc feature gating). **Suite/lane fit:** shared infra for any Vitest suite honoring `.feat.<featureId>.` filenames. **Wiring status:** confirmed executed (imported by multiple Vitest configs including `vitest.config.ts`, `apps/ui/vitest*.config.ts`, `apps/cli/vitest*.config.ts`, `apps/server/vitest*.config.ts`).
- [x] `vitest.config.ts` — **What it covers:** root Vitest guardrail (ad-hoc root runs): sets node env, `globals:false`, forces `HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV=''`, and excludes `.project/**`/`node_modules/**`/`dist/**` plus feature-gated globs from `resolveVitestFeatureTestExcludeGlobs()`. **Real behavior vs mocks:** config-only. **Brittleness risks:** low–medium (exclude list must track any new ephemeral dirs; feature-gating globs depend on filename convention). **Speed/flakiness risks:** none. **Duplication candidates:** consolidate “exclude local dirs” policy across configs to avoid drift. **Suite/lane fit:** infra safety net (not a CI lane). **Wiring status:** confirmed executed only when developers run `vitest` from repo root (CI/lane scripts use package-local configs).
- [x] `packages/tests/scripts/run-vitest-with-heartbeat.mjs` — **What it covers:** Vitest runner wrapper for `@happier-dev/tests`: requires `--config <vitest.*.config.ts>`, runs `yarn -s vitest run --no-file-parallelism -c <config> …`, emits periodic “still running” heartbeats controlled by `HAPPIER_TEST_HEARTBEAT_MS` (default `30000`, min `1000`), forwards `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`/`SIGHUP`, and exits with the child code. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real subprocess spawn + logging; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium (forces `--no-file-parallelism`; signal forwarding doesn’t guarantee full kill-tree cleanup if the child spawns grandchildren). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium (determinism tradeoff can slow suites; heartbeat is stable). **Duplication candidates:** overlaps other runner scripts’ spawn/signal/timeout patterns; standardize on one runner harness + `processTree`. **Suite/lane fit:** infra runner for long-running Vitest lanes (core/providers/stress). **Wiring status:** confirmed executed via `packages/tests/package.json` scripts (`test`, `test:core:*`, `test:providers`, `test:stress`) and thus by CI.
- [x] `packages/tests/scripts/run-providers.mjs` — **What it covers:** providers lane orchestrator (`yarn providers:run <preset> <tier>`): validates flags, resolves preset env via `resolveProviderRunPreset`, defaults DB provider to sqlite when unset (`HAPPIER_E2E_DB_PROVIDER`/`HAPPY_E2E_DB_PROVIDER`), sets provider knobs (`HAPPIER_E2E_PROVIDER_UPDATE_BASELINES`, `HAPPIER_E2E_PROVIDER_STRICT_KEYS`, `HAPPIER_E2E_PROVIDER_FLAKE_RETRY`), enforces a watchdog (`HAPPIER_E2E_PROVIDER_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`/`HAPPY_E2E_PROVIDER_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`), and kills the child tree via `terminateProcessTreeByPid`. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real subprocess spawn + kill-tree; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium (env/flag contract sprawl; relies on detached process groups for POSIX kill-by-group). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium (long-running suites + hard timeout; kill timing can be flaky on Windows). **Duplication candidates:** shares spawn/signal/timeout logic with other runners; centralize. **Suite/lane fit:** provider contract lane entrypoint (orchestration). **Wiring status:** confirmed executed via `packages/tests/package.json` (`providers:run` + provider preset scripts) and root `yarn test:providers*` entrypoints.
- [x] `packages/tests/scripts/run-providers-parallel.mjs` — **What it covers:** parallel provider orchestrator (`yarn providers:run:parallel`): selects providers by preset + optional scenario selection (`HAPPIER_E2E_PROVIDER_SCENARIOS`/`HAPPY_E2E_PROVIDER_SCENARIOS`), runs with concurrency (`--max-parallel`, default `4`), prewarms server provider generation (`CI=1`, `PORT=0`, `PUBLIC_URL`, dummy `DATABASE_URL`, `HAPPIER_BUILD_DB_PROVIDERS`), writes failure reports (`HAPPIER_E2E_PROVIDER_FAILURE_REPORT_PATH`) + token ledgers (`HAPPIER_E2E_PROVIDER_TOKEN_LEDGER_PATH`) under `.project/logs/e2e/<runId>/…`, and optionally retries failures serially (including targeted “scenario tail” retry). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real subprocess spawn + filesystem I/O; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** high (many env knobs; relies on `providerScenarios.json` shape + token ledger schema pins). **Speed/flakiness risks:** high (parallel contention; teardown timing; Windows process termination). **Duplication candidates:** token-ledger merge/summary logic duplicates other scripts/harness; extract canonical ledger library + runner harness. **Suite/lane fit:** providers tooling (heavy orchestration; opt-in). **Wiring status:** confirmed wired via `packages/tests/package.json` (`providers:run:parallel`, `providers:all:*:parallel`) (typically manual/opt-in).

## Unit — packages/protocol (Vitest)

- **Runner:** Vitest
- **Commands:** `yarn workspace @happier-dev/protocol test`, `yarn test:unit`
- **Config files:** `packages/protocol/package.json`
- **Includes:** Vitest defaults (package-local; **confirmed** for Vitest `^3.2.x` via `node_modules/vitest/dist/config.cjs#defaultInclude`): `**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)`
- **Excludes:** `node_modules`, `dist`, `coverage`, dot-folders (Vitest defaults); plus `packages/protocol/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/**/*.test.ts` + `src/**/*.spec.ts` from the pretest `tsc` build`
- **Known env vars:** `HAPPIER_REQUIRE_FEATURE_POLICY`, `HAPPIER_EMBEDDED_POLICY_ENV` (consumed by pretest build generation script)
- **CI entrypoints (grep):**
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:255:        run: yarn workspace @happier-dev/protocol test`
- **Notes:**
  - Package name: @happier-dev/protocol
  - **Important wiring detail:** `packages/protocol/package.json` runs `pretest` → `yarn -s build` (generator + `tsc`) before `vitest run`. This catches type errors in `src/**/*.ts` (excluding tests) but adds fixed cost to every test run.

### Test files
- [x] `packages/agents/src/providers/cliInstallSpecs.spec.ts` — **What it covers:** provider CLI install-spec registry invariants: every `AGENT_IDS` entry maps to an install spec with matching `id` and at least one binary; known providers’ specs include expected upstream install hints (URLs/package names) embedded somewhere in the spec. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real `AGENT_IDS` and real `getProviderCliInstallSpec`; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium–high (asserts raw substrings like `claude.ai/install.sh`, npm package names; will churn on upstream doc/URL changes or copy edits; `JSON.stringify` is an implementation-ish way to search). **Speed/flakiness risks:** low. **Duplication candidates:** overlaps with provider install/availability tests elsewhere (notably `packages/cli-common/tests/providers.test.mjs`); candidate to centralize “provider install hint contract” in one package and have others import the canonical data. **Suite/lane fit:** unit/registry guardrail (UX/ops contract). **Wiring status:** confirmed executed by agents Vitest lane (`yarn workspace @happier-dev/agents test`) as part of root `yarn test:unit` / CI unit workflow.
- [x] `packages/agents/src/sessionControls/publish.spec.ts` — **What it covers:** session-controls publish semantics: monotonic updatedAt policy (`ignore_older` applies newer and drops stale; `force_update` bumps timestamp only when value changes), permission intent metadata update (`computeNextPermissionIntentMetadata` rejects invalid permissionMode tokens but persists canonical tokens), and metadata string override tombstones (`computeNextMetadataStringOverrideV1` trims whitespace→null and monotonic-bumps when clearing with stale updatedAt). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real pure functions; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** low–medium (pins exact timestamp bump math and null-tombstone shape). **Speed/flakiness risks:** low. **Duplication candidates:** monotonic “updatedAt bump” logic likely repeats in other domains (settings/overrides); consider extracting a shared monotonic helper (and test once) if multiple packages need identical semantics. **Suite/lane fit:** unit/contract (core correctness). **Wiring status:** confirmed executed by agents Vitest lane via root `yarn test:unit` / CI unit workflow.
- [x] `packages/agents/src/sessions/replay/happierReplayPrompt.spec.ts` — **What it covers:** replay prompt rendering invariants: `buildHappierReplayPromptFromDialog` includes a stable header with previous session id, includes only the most recent `recentMessagesCount` dialog items (excludes earlier ones), formats role prefixes (`User:`/`Assistant:`), and drops empty/whitespace-only dialog text. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real prompt builder; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium (asserts prompt substrings and formatting/copy like “Previous session id:” and “Recent transcript:”; will churn on prompt copy/format refactors). **Speed/flakiness risks:** low. **Duplication candidates:** similar prompt-string tests exist across agents/CLI; consider asserting structured intermediate representation (selected dialog items) and leaving final formatting to a smaller “formatting smoke” test. **Suite/lane fit:** unit/prompt contract. **Wiring status:** confirmed executed by agents Vitest lane via root `yarn test:unit` / CI unit workflow.
- [x] `packages/agents/src/voice/voiceAgentPrompt.spec.ts` — **What it covers:** voice prompt/spec alignment: ElevenLabs prompt includes every voice tool-action spec’s `voiceClientToolName` and (when present) its `argsExample`; disabled action ids are omitted; local voice system prompt includes all voice action-block specs’ tool names and omits disabled ones; also asserts local prompt includes `VOICE_TOOL_RESULTS_JSON:` marker. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real prompt builders + real protocol spec enumerators (`listVoiceToolActionSpecs`, `listVoiceActionBlockSpecs`); no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium–high (asserts raw substrings; prompt formatting changes will churn; uses `as any` casts to pass `disabledActionIds`). **Speed/flakiness risks:** low. **Duplication candidates:** overlaps other “prompt must include all specs” tests; could share a helper that asserts “all spec toolNames present except disabled” and reuse across prompt variants. **Suite/lane fit:** unit/contract bridging protocol↔agents (high-signal drift guard). **Wiring status:** confirmed executed by agents Vitest lane via root `yarn test:unit` / CI unit workflow.

High dedupe value: centralize common “screen render + router + storage” harness and reduce per-file mocking boilerplate.
- [x] Spot-check for internal mocks (disallowed) vs boundary mocks (allowed) — Boundary mocks are common/expected (global `fetch`, storage globals, native modules). **Internal mocks are widespread** in `apps/ui/sources/__tests__/app/**` (mocking `@/sync/*`, hooks, components) which lowers confidence and creates patchwork wiring tests; many of these could be refactored into pure-function tests at the domain layer with far fewer mocks.
- [x] Identify brittle assertions (copy/snapshots/time/ordering/impl details) — Hotspots: referential-identity assertions (e.g. “request object is stable”), “setOptions loop”/navigation sequencing, prompt/copy substring pins, and tests that assert exact “stack options” objects. Favor behavior/outcome assertions (navigation intent, state transitions, returned data) over identity/equality of intermediate props.
- [x] Identify slow/flaky tests and root causes (timeouts, orchestration, parallelism) — Infra already signals risk: pool forced to `forks`, `testTimeout=20s`, and per-file isolation; `apps/ui/sources/dev/vitestSetup.ts` includes guardrails for timer leakage + global unstubbing. Likely slowest/flakiest: react-test-renderer + async `act` microtask flushing + heavy mocking; parallelism capped via `VITEST_UI_MAX_FORKS` to stabilize.
- [x] Identify duplication/over-testing and consolidation opportunities — Repeated “presentation” tests across pickers/screens, repeated router + unistyles + RN stub scaffolding, and multiple tests for stability/identity of props. Consolidate via shared harness + prefer testing the pure builders/selectors (options derivation, request building) once, then keep only a small number of high-signal screen tests for key flows.
- [x] Confirm CI wiring runs this suite at the right times (PR, release, nightly) — CI default gate runs UI unit + integration in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (invokes `yarn workspace @happier-dev/app test:unit` + `test:integration`). UI release workflows also run `apps/ui test:unit` + `test:integration` (`promote-ui.yml`). ## Integration — apps/ui (Vitest)

- **Runner:** Vitest
- **Commands:** `yarn --cwd apps/ui test:integration`, `yarn workspace @happier-dev/app test:integration`, `yarn test:integration`
- **Config files:** `apps/ui/vitest.integration.config.ts`, `apps/ui/vitest.config.ts`
- **Includes:** `sources/**/*.integration.*`, `sources/**/*.e2e.test.*`
- **Excludes:** `feature-gated globs`
- **Known env vars:** `HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV`
- **CI entrypoints (grep):**
  - `.github/workflows/promote-ui.yml:303:          yarn --cwd apps/ui test:unit`
  - `.github/workflows/promote-ui.yml:304:          yarn --cwd apps/ui test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/release-npm.yml:268:          yarn --cwd apps/cli test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/release-npm.yml:274:          yarn --cwd apps/stack test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:301:        run: yarn --cwd apps/server test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:480:        run: yarn --cwd apps/stack test:integration`

- [x] `apps/ui/sources/sync/ops/sessions.scm.integration.test.ts` — **What it covers:** integration of `sessionScm*` ops for git backend: injects `backendPreference` from local settings (prefer sapling), stages/commits/log-lists via session RPC, discards modified+untracked entries, atomic `all-pending` commit includes tracked + untracked, remote `fetch` against a real bare remote, push rejection when behind (non-fast-forward), pull rejection when worktree dirty, push success when ahead, pull rejection when non-FF-only required, upstream-required errors when remote/branch missing, explicit remote/branch override behavior, detached-HEAD push/pull guards, patch-apply failure mapping, safe NOT_REPOSITORY behavior (snapshot returns `isRepo:false`), transport failure mapping to `COMMAND_FAILED`, and commit backout/revert behavior (success, dirty-worktree block, merge-commit deterministic error, detached-HEAD block). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real git CLI + filesystem via `createGitSessionRpcHarness`; boundary mock for session RPC transport; minimal sync encryption stub; uses real storage setting injection. **Brittleness risks:** medium: relies on git CLI behavior and some message substrings (e.g. “revert”, “merge commit”) and on error-code mappings; a number of tests are essentially “call shape + error mapping” rather than user-observable UI outcomes. **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium–high: many tests spin up repos and remotes; process-heavy and can be slow under CI; appropriate for integration lane but overlaps with hook-level SCM integration coverage. **Duplication candidates:** significant overlap with `useFilesScmOperations.integration.test.ts` and other SCM integration tests (remote fetch/push/pull semantics, upstream-required errors, commit creation); consider choosing a single canonical integration layer (either ops-level or hook-level) and moving the other layer toward smaller unit tests to avoid duplicated slow coverage. **Suite/lane fit:** integration. **Wiring status:** executed by `apps/ui/vitest.integration.config.ts` and CI `ui` integration job.

## Unit — apps/cli (Vitest)

- **Runner:** Vitest
- **Commands:** `yarn --cwd apps/cli test:unit`, `yarn workspace @happier-dev/cli test:unit`, `yarn test:unit`
- **Config files:** `apps/cli/vitest.config.ts`, `apps/cli/src/vitestSetup.ts`, `apps/cli/src/test-setup.ts`
- **Includes:** `src/**/*.test.ts`, `scripts/**/*.test.ts`
- **Excludes:** `**/*.slow.test.ts`, `**/*.integration.*`, `**/*.e2e.test.ts`, `feature-gated globs`
- **Known env vars:** `HAPPIER_SERVER_URL`, `HAPPIER_WEBAPP_URL`, `HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV`
- **CI entrypoints (grep):**
  - `.github/workflows/promote-ui.yml:303:          yarn --cwd apps/ui test:unit`
  - `.github/workflows/release-npm.yml:267:          yarn --cwd apps/cli test:unit`
  - `.github/workflows/release-npm.yml:268:          yarn --cwd apps/cli test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/release-npm.yml:273:          yarn --cwd apps/stack test:unit`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:298:        run: yarn --cwd apps/server test:unit`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:477:        run: yarn --cwd apps/stack test:unit`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:1111:          yarn --cwd apps/cli -s vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts src/daemon/daemon.integration.test.ts`

## Integration — apps/cli (Vitest)

- **Runner:** Vitest
- **Commands:** `yarn --cwd apps/cli test:integration`, `yarn workspace @happier-dev/cli test:integration`, `yarn test:integration`
- **Config files:** `apps/cli/vitest.integration.config.ts`, `apps/cli/src/test-setup.ts`
- **Includes:** `src/**/*.integration.*`, `src/**/*.e2e.test.ts`, `scripts/**/*.integration.test.ts`
- **Excludes:** `feature-gated globs`
- **Known env vars:** `HAPPIER_SERVER_URL`, `HAPPIER_WEBAPP_URL`, `HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV`
- **CI entrypoints (grep):**
  - `.github/workflows/promote-ui.yml:304:          yarn --cwd apps/ui test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/release-npm.yml:268:          yarn --cwd apps/cli test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/release-npm.yml:274:          yarn --cwd apps/stack test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:301:        run: yarn --cwd apps/server test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:480:        run: yarn --cwd apps/stack test:integration`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:1111:          yarn --cwd apps/cli -s vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts src/daemon/daemon.integration.test.ts`

## Unit — apps/server (Vitest)

- **Runner:** Vitest
- **Commands:** `yarn --cwd apps/server test:unit`, `yarn test:unit`
- **Config files:** `apps/server/vitest.config.ts`
- **Includes:** `sources/**/*.test.ts`, `sources/**/*.spec.ts`, `scripts/**/*.test.ts`, `scripts/**/*.spec.ts`
- **Excludes:** `**/*.dbcontract.spec.ts`, `**/*.integration.*`, `**/*.real.integration.test.ts`, `feature-gated globs`

- [x] `apps/server/package.json` — **What it covers:** server workspace lifecycle + lane wiring: declares `test:unit` (`vitest … -c vitest.config.ts`), `test:integration` (`vitest … -c vitest.integration.config.ts`), `test:db-contract`, plus `pretest` hook (`build:shared` + `schema:sync:check`) and local dev helpers (migrations/generate, docker helpers for postgres/redis/minio + `s3:init`, `validate:redis-adapter`). **Real behavior vs mocks:** N/A (package scripts/config), but it **invokes real subprocesses** (`node`, `yarn`, `prisma`, `docker`, `dotenv`) and relies on external tools being available. **Brittleness risks:** medium–high: `pretest` couples tests to schema sync state; docker scripts assume host docker + fixed ports (5432/6379/9000/9001); `postinstall` is a large inline script with gating logic and can be hard to debug; migrations/scripts rely on `.env.dev` and Prisma schema paths. **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium: `pretest` adds fixed overhead; integration/db-contract lanes can be slow due to migrations and external services. **Duplication candidates:** workspace-level `postinstall` gating + docker helper scripts likely repeat across workspaces; consider centralizing shared patterns in `scripts/` (while keeping workspace-specific knobs). **Suite/lane fit:** infra/wiring (authoritative entrypoint for server test lanes). **Wiring status:** confirmed executed via repo root scripts (`yarn test:unit` runs `yarn --cwd apps/server test:unit`; `yarn test:integration` runs `yarn --cwd apps/server test:integration`).
- [x] `apps/server/sources/app/api/utils/enableAuthentication.ts` — **What it covers:** production auth decorator helper for Fastify: installs `authenticate` that requires `Authorization: Bearer …`, verifies via `auth.verifyToken`, enforces login eligibility via `enforceLoginEligibility({ accountId, env: process.env })`, and returns structured error payloads (`missing header`, `invalid-token`, `provider-required`, `account-disabled`, `not-eligible`, etc). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real implementation (no mocks in-module), but callers/tests often stub env and/or rely on real `auth` init/token creation. **Brittleness risks:** medium: logs on every auth check (tests must avoid asserting on log output); error payload shapes are effectively API contracts and can churn if not treated as such. **Speed/flakiness risks:** low–medium: calls into token verification + eligibility checks (may touch DB depending on eligibility path). **Duplication candidates:** several integration specs re-implement ad-hoc `decorate('authenticate', …)`; prefer consistently using this helper or a single test-only variant when full eligibility enforcement is not desired. **Suite/lane fit:** production helper used by multiple integration specs as test plumbing. **Wiring status:** executed indirectly via routes/apps that call `enableAuthentication` (confirmed imported by multiple `apps/server` integration specs).

## Integration — apps/server (Vitest)

- **Runner:** Vitest
- **Commands:** `yarn --cwd apps/server test:integration`, `yarn test:integration`
- **Config files:** `apps/server/vitest.integration.config.ts`
- **Includes:** `sources/**/*.integration.*`, `scripts/**/*.integration.*`
- **Excludes:** `feature-gated globs`
- **Known env vars:** `HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV`
- **CI entrypoints (grep):**
  - `.github/workflows/extended-db-tests.yml:200:        run: yarn --cwd apps/server test:db-contract`

- [x] Spot-check for internal mocks (disallowed) vs boundary mocks (allowed) — `suites/core-e2e/**` contains **no `vi.mock(...)`** patterns (grep) and generally runs real components. Some support/infra tests (e.g. `cliDist.sharedDeps.test.ts`) use `vi.fn`/module reload to stub the OS boundary “run yarn build” step; this is an allowed boundary mock to keep the lane deterministic. Most e2e tests use **boundary fakes** via real executables/scripts (fake Claude/Codex/ACP agents) rather than mocking internal domain logic.
- [x] Identify brittle assertions (copy/snapshots/time/ordering/impl details) — Brittleness mostly comes from (1) asserting on **CLI argv details** and internal hook flags (e.g. `--settings`, `--input-format`), (2) parsing tool/provider **JSONL logs** and transcript payload shapes, (3) time-based behavior validated via **fixed delays** (`sleep(...)`) or polling windows, and (4) relying on exact route payload shapes/state strings (`queued|running|succeeded`, pairing states, change-hint shapes). These are appropriate for e2e regressions but should be limited to stable contracts (prefer schema parsing where available, avoid pinning incidental copy).
- [x] Identify slow/flaky tests and root causes (timeouts, orchestration, parallelism) — Hotspots are multi-process tests that build/run the CLI and manage daemons/tmux/sockets (Claude/Codex switching, ACP steering). Flake drivers: port allocation/OS scheduling, filesystem timing (log files appearing), long build steps, and fixed sleeps near lease boundaries. Stability mitigations present: wrapper forces `--no-file-parallelism`, slow lane sets `fileParallelism:false`, timeouts are high (180s). **Potential misfit:** some “fast-start” tests (`claude.fastStart...`, `codex.fastStart...`) intentionally inject long create-session delays and may be too slow/flake-prone for the fast lane.
- [x] Identify duplication/over-testing and consolidation opportunities — Significant duplication across core-e2e files: ad-hoc `requestJson(...)` wrappers, repeated `writeTestManifestForServer` + `FailureArtifacts` patterns, repeated env-building for CLI processes, and repeated “decrypt transcript then `asRecord/asArray` parse” helpers. Consolidation: extract a core-e2e harness + shared request helper; consider relocating truly unit-only tests (e.g. baseline shape scoring) to the providers/unit lane if they don’t need server-light.
- [x] Confirm CI wiring runs this suite at the right times (PR, release, nightly) — **PR/push:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml` job `e2e-core` runs `yarn test:e2e:core:fast` (sqlite) with `CI=1`, `HAPPIER_E2E_DB_PROVIDER=sqlite`, `HAPPIER_E2E_SAVE_ARTIFACTS=0` (so **non-`.slow` core-e2e tests** run on PR/push). **Slow lane:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml` job `e2e-core-slow` exists but runs only on `workflow_call` when `inputs.run_e2e_core_slow` is true (not on PR by default). **Nightly/manual extended DB:** `.github/workflows/extended-db-tests.yml` (schedule + workflow_dispatch) runs `yarn test:e2e` against **Postgres and MySQL** with `DATABASE_URL` set; this invokes `packages/tests` base core config (so it includes `*.slow.e2e.test.ts` as well as non-slow tests). **Dead/unwired:** none observed; “slow” tests are skipped in PR fast lane but executed by extended DB matrix and/or optional workflow_call slow job.

### Test files

- [x] `packages/tests/src/testkit/cliAccessKey.spec.ts` — **What it covers:** `readCliAccessKey(homeDir)` selection rules: prefers per-server `servers/<activeServerId>/access.key` when `settings.json` (schema v5) points to it; otherwise falls back to newest `servers/*/access.key` by mtime; exercises both legacy `{token,secret}` and newer `{token,encryption:{publicKey,machineKey}}` shapes. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real filesystem writes/reads under a temp run dir (`createRunDirs`); no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium (mtime-based “newest file” ordering is enforced via `setTimeout(10)`; can flake on coarse timestamp filesystems or heavy CI load; pins on-disk directory layout). **Speed/flakiness risks:** low–medium (FS I/O + small timer). **Duplication candidates:** overlaps “activeServerId from settings + fallback scan” patterns with `packages/tests/src/testkit/daemon/daemon.statePath.spec.ts`; consider a shared testkit builder for “home dir with servers + settings” and explicit mtime control. **Suite/lane fit:** unit-ish infra test (supports core-e2e harness correctness). **Wiring status:** confirmed executed (explicitly allowlisted in `packages/tests/vitest.core.config.ts` and `packages/tests/vitest.core.fast.config.ts`).
- [x] `packages/tests/src/testkit/daemon/daemon.statePath.spec.ts` — **What it covers:** `readDaemonState(homeDir)` discovery/backcompat: reads `servers/<activeServerId>/daemon.state.json` when `settings.json` schema v5 selects a server; supports legacy `daemon.state.json` at home root; falls back to scanning `servers/*/daemon.state.json` when settings selection points elsewhere (e.g. cloud) but state exists for another server id. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real filesystem layout under `mkdtemp`; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium (pins home-dir layout + settings.json schema fields/semantics; assumes JSON structure includes `pid`/`httpPort`). **Speed/flakiness risks:** low (temp FS only). **Duplication candidates:** overlaps with `cliAccessKey.spec.ts` selection logic; candidate for shared “resolveActiveServerId + fallback scan” utility and shared fixtures. **Suite/lane fit:** unit-ish infra/backcompat test (appropriate for core-e2e support). **Wiring status:** confirmed executed (explicitly allowlisted in `packages/tests/vitest.core.config.ts` and `packages/tests/vitest.core.fast.config.ts`).

### Support/infra files (configs, setup, fixtures, testkit)

- [x] `packages/tests/package.json` — **What it covers:** wiring/entrypoints for `@happier-dev/tests`: Vitest core lanes (`test`, `test:core:fast`, `test:core:slow`, `test:stress`, `test:providers`), Playwright UI e2e (`test:ui:e2e`), and provider-runner CLIs (`providers:run`, per-provider shortcuts, parallel runner, token ledger summary). Declares runtime deps (`socket.io-client`, `tweetnacl`, `privacy-kit`) and dev deps (`vitest`, `@playwright/test`, `typescript`). **Real behavior vs mocks:** not a test; it configures how suites run (no mocks). **Brittleness risks:** medium: scripts hardcode config filenames and use node runner wrappers; long list of per-provider scripts duplicates provider catalog and can drift when providers are added/renamed (also includes `providers:pi:*` despite presets list elsewhere not mentioning pi). **Speed/flakiness risks:** indirect: lane selection affects parallelism/timeouts (core uses heartbeat wrapper; Playwright uses single worker). **Duplication candidates:** per-provider script explosion is largely duplicative; could be replaced with a single `providers:run <provider> <tier>` and a generated script list (or rely on `providers:run` only). **Suite/lane fit:** infra file defining lane contracts; critical to discovery/wiring. **Wiring status:** confirmed executed by CI lanes that call `yarn workspace @happier-dev/tests test:*` and root `yarn test:e2e:*` scripts (not dead).

- [x] `packages/tests/scripts/processTree.mjs` — **What it covers:** cross-platform best-effort process-tree termination for scripts: detects liveness (`kill(pid,0)`), terminates via process group (`kill(-pid, SIGTERM/SIGKILL)`) with PID fallback, uses Windows `taskkill /T /F`, and polls until grace timeout before SIGKILL. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real OS process/signals; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium–high: process-group semantics require detached/spawned group leadership; negative-pid kill is OS-dependent; Windows relies on `COMSPEC`/`taskkill`. **Speed/flakiness risks:** low–medium: polling loop up to `graceMs` (default 10s) can slow shutdown in failure cases. **Duplication candidates:** likely duplicates kill-tree logic elsewhere in repo; centralize one helper to avoid divergence. **Suite/lane fit:** infra/orchestration helper (used by provider runners and any timeout logic). **Wiring status:** imported and exercised by `run-providers*.mjs` (and anything else that needs kill-tree); not dead.

- [x] `packages/tests/src/testkit/updates.ts` — **What it covers:** small socket-update assertions: counts and checks for `update` events whose body is `{t:'new-message'}` and whose message has the given `localId`. **Real behavior vs mocks:** pure filtering over captured socket events; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium: pins update body shape (`t:'new-message'`) and message structure; ignores protocol evolution (new body kinds). **Speed/flakiness risks:** none (pure); callers’ event collection timing is the flake vector. **Duplication candidates:** similar “find update event by predicate” patterns exist in tests; consider a generic `findUpdateEvents({ t, predicate })` helper. **Suite/lane fit:** socket-test helper for e2e. **Wiring status:** used by socket-driven e2e tests (import-based); not dead.
- [x] `packages/tests/src/testkit/waitForRegexInFile.ts` — **What it covers:** polls a file until a regex matches: repeatedly reads file text and matches a non-global cloned regex, using shared `waitFor` for timeout/interval; on failure includes a 4k tail for diagnostics. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real filesystem reads + polling; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium: log/regex coupling (format changes break waits); repeated full-file reads can be inefficient for large logs; cloning regex drops `g` but preserves other flags. **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium: polling loop defaults 60s/100ms; can add IO pressure and flake if log writes are delayed. **Duplication candidates:** duplicates other “wait for substring/regex in log” logic (fakeClaude, uiWeb baseUrl stdout parsing); centralize a tailing/seek-based log waiter. **Suite/lane fit:** infra helper (e2e process/log orchestration). **Wiring status:** used by CLI terminal connect helper and likely other process harnesses; not dead.

### Test files

- [x] `packages/tests/suites/stress/reconnect.chaos.test.ts` — **What it covers:** seeded reconnection chaos against a real server: drives two socket clients through randomized disconnect/reconnect scenarios (`b-offline`, `both-drop`, `b-flap`), sends many messages from A (with occasional same-`localId` resend to simulate retry noise), then asserts transcript convergence invariants (no duplicate localIds, all expected seqs present, max seq advanced, and recent localIds present). Also writes run manifests + captures failure artifacts and can classify “flaky” via one retry when `HAPPIER_E2E_FLAKE_RETRY` is enabled. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real `startServerLight` + real socket.io + real protocol ack schema parse; only deterministic RNG helpers (no mocks). **Brittleness risks:** high (randomized message counts and timing; hard-coupled to socket ack schema + `didWrite` idempotency semantics; assertions depend on eventual transcript catch-up behavior). **Speed/flakiness risks:** very high (orchestration heavy; loops `HAPPIER_E2E_REPEAT`; multiple 20s connect waits + sleeps; susceptible to CI jitter and reconnect race conditions). **Duplication candidates:** overlaps `reconnect.repeat.test.ts` scaffolding and core-e2e reconnect/message invariants; extract a shared harness + invariant checker. **Suite/lane fit:** stress/chaos lane (correct). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `packages/tests/vitest.stress.config.ts` + `packages/tests/package.json` `test:stress`; CI wiring is opt-in (`tests.yml` `stress` job).
- [x] `packages/tests/suites/stress/reconnect.repeat.test.ts` — **What it covers:** deterministic reconnect repeat loop: for N repeats, creates a session, connects two sockets, sends 5 messages with B disconnected mid-stream, reconnects B, then asserts transcript head convergence invariants (length ≥ sent, no duplicate localIds, all expected seqs + localIds present). Captures artifacts + run manifest per iteration. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real server + sockets + protocol ack schema; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium–high (depends on socket connect/disconnect readiness and transcript catch-up; asserts exact membership of seq/localId). **Speed/flakiness risks:** high (real orchestration; repeats default 5; connect waits up to 20s; transcript fetch). **Duplication candidates:** shares most scaffolding with `reconnect.chaos.test.ts`; consolidate setup + invariant checks. **Suite/lane fit:** stress lane (correct). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `packages/tests/vitest.stress.config.ts` + `yarn workspace @happier-dev/tests test:stress` (CI opt-in).

## UI E2E — packages/tests (Playwright)

- **Runner:** @playwright/test
- **Commands:** `yarn workspace @happier-dev/tests test:ui:e2e`, `yarn test:e2e:ui`
- **Config files:** `packages/tests/playwright.ui.config.mjs`
- **Includes:** `suites/ui-e2e/**/*.spec.ts`
- **Known env vars:** (see “Enumerate env vars…” in Suite audit TODO below; large set including `CI`, `HOME`, `PATH`, `PWD`/`OLDPWD`, `TERM`/`NO_COLOR`, many `HAPPIER_STACK_*` and `HAPPIER_*` auth/server flags)
- **CI entrypoints (grep):**
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:201:        run: yarn -s test:e2e:ui`

- [x] `packages/tests/suites/ui-e2e/auth.oauth.provisioningChoice.optional.plain.github.spec.ts` — **What it covers:** UI-e2e OAuth provisioning choice (GitHub) on optional storage policy: starts server-light with keyless OAuth enabled + auto-provision and default account mode `e2ee`, starts Expo web UI, clicks provider signup, asserts both provisioning choice buttons appear (`oauth-provisioning-choice-plain` + `...-e2ee`), selects plaintext, waits for `/v1/auth/external/github/finalize-keyless` 200, lands on `/` and “connect machine” getting-started state, and validates persistence via sqlite queries (GitHub AccountIdentity exists; Account `publicKey is null` and `encryptionMode='plain'`). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real server-light + real UI web + real Playwright browser; boundary fakes: `startFakeGitHubOAuthServer` (OAuth/API boundary), port reservation, and sqlite DB introspection via `sqlite3 -json`. **Brittleness risks:** high: pins UI `data-testid`s, finalize-keyless endpoint path/status, server-light sqlite DB filename/location, DB table/column names, and requires `sqlite3` on PATH. **Speed/flakiness risks:** very high (multi-process orchestration + serial mode + long timeouts + response waiters; port reservation and startup timing are common flake sources). **Duplication candidates:** repeats patterns from other OAuth UI-e2e specs (oauth fake server, `reserveAvailablePort`, sqlite query helpers, server-light env matrices); extract shared helpers/presets to reduce drift. **Suite/lane fit:** UI E2E (auth) is correct; too orchestration-heavy for unit/integration lanes. **Wiring status:** executed by Playwright UI lane (`packages/tests/playwright.ui.config.mjs` `testDir:suites/ui-e2e`) and CI `ui-e2e` job (paths-filtered/opt-in via `workflow_call` inputs).
