- [x] Identify brittle assertions (copy/snapshots/time/ordering/impl details) — Several tests pin **help/usage text** and stderr substrings (e.g. `auth --help`, `doctor` messages, “--flow is no longer supported”), plus assert exact JSON fields (`flow`, `cmd`, `configureServer.*`) and hardcoded URL formatting (`http://localhost:<port>`). Risks: copy churn, output formatting changes, and OS path differences (some assertions expect `/main/env` suffix).
- [x] Identify slow/flaky tests and root causes (timeouts, orchestration, parallelism) — Spawning `node` repeatedly + filesystem temp dirs is moderate cost; flake risks include (1) sandbox/CI restrictions on binding loopback ports (`auth_login_guided_server_no_expo.test.mjs` explicitly skips on `EPERM`), (2) global `process.env` / `process.chdir` mutation (`ci.test.mjs`) if the node:test runner parallelizes files, (3) reliance on `git` being available + fast (`daemon_dist_guard.test.mjs`), and (4) detached child processes + `process.kill` semantics (daemon stubs).
- [x] Identify duplication/over-testing and consolidation opportunities — Repeated patterns across many files: `spawn` wrappers that capture stdout/stderr, repeated stack env fixture lines (`HAPPIER_STACK_TAILSCALE_*` toggles), and repeated “minimal monorepo” scaffolds (create `apps/{ui,cli,server}` placeholders). Consolidate into `testkit/*` helpers and/or table-driven matrices to reduce drift.
- [x] Confirm CI wiring runs this suite at the right times (PR, release, nightly) — Confirmed wired in PR CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml:477` runs `yarn --cwd apps/stack test:unit`) and release pipeline (`.github/workflows/release-npm.yml:273`). Integration and real-integration stacks are wired separately in the same workflows (see grep list above), so `.integration.test.mjs` exclusions here do not imply “dead tests”.

### Test files

- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_force_flag.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** `--force` CLI flag resolution (`resolveAuthForceFlag`) and env export behavior (`applyAuthForceEnv` sets `HAPPIER_AUTH_FORCE=1`). **Real behavior vs mocks:** pure arg/env logic; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** low (pins flag name + env var key). **Speed/flakiness risks:** none. **Duplication candidates:** could be table-driven with other flag/env resolvers; small. **Suite/lane fit:** true unit test (appropriate for `test:unit`). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `apps/stack/scripts/test_ci.mjs` (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_help_cmd.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** `hstack auth --help` output includes seed/dev-auth subcommands and auth-login targeting flags (`--webapp*`, `--method`, `--start-if-needed`). **Real behavior vs mocks:** spawns real `node` against `apps/stack/bin/hstack.mjs` via `auth_testkit` (boundary: subprocess); relies on env overrides to avoid loading real user stack env. **Brittleness risks:** high (pins help/usage copy + flag spelling/ordering). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium (subprocess spawn + stdout matching). **Duplication candidates:** help/usage assertions similar across other command help tests; centralize a “help contains flags” helper. **Suite/lane fit:** closer to CLI integration than pure unit, but still hermetic; consider moving slow/help-heavy tests behind a “cli-contract” subgroup if lane time grows. **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_login_flow_in_tty.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** auth login flow selection in TTY context: default `guided` flow in `--print --json`, `--method=mobile` preserves guided, and `--flow` overrides are rejected (including invalid values). **Real behavior vs mocks:** spawns `hstack` via `auth_testkit` (boundary subprocess + temp FS stack fixture). **Brittleness risks:** medium–high (pins JSON field `flow` and stderr text “--flow is no longer supported”). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium (multiple subprocess runs + temp dirs). **Duplication candidates:** repeated stack env lines + `runNodeCapture` usage across auth tests; fold into shared auth-login matrix helper. **Suite/lane fit:** integration-ish (CLI invocation), but scoped and hermetic. **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_login_force_default.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** `hstack auth login` printed command: omits `--force` by default, includes `--force` when requested, and includes stable server scope env (`HAPPIER_ACTIVE_SERVER_ID="stack_main__id_default"`). **Real behavior vs mocks:** subprocess via `auth_testkit` + temp stack fixture; no internal mocks. **Brittleness risks:** high (asserts on formatted shell `cmd` string; quoting/spacing changes will churn). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium (subprocess + temp FS). **Duplication candidates:** `--print --json` parsing/assertion repeated across auth tests; share a helper to parse/normalize `cmd`. **Suite/lane fit:** CLI contract test (integration-ish). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_login_guided_server_no_expo.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** guided web auth fails closed when Expo UI is not ready: attempts background UI start, reports diagnostics (runtime path + server health), and **does not** fall back to printing a server URL. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real local HTTP server (`/health`) + real temp FS “minimal monorepo” + boundary stub of `apps/cli/bin/happier.mjs` to keep test non-interactive; skips on sandbox `EPERM` for binding ports. **Brittleness risks:** high (pins multiple stderr substrings + relies on specific diagnostic phrasing). **Speed/flakiness risks:** high-ish (network port bind, subprocess, timing with `HAPPIER_STACK_AUTH_UI_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=1`). **Duplication candidates:** “minimal monorepo stub” appears in multiple tests; consolidate into `auth_testkit` fixture builder. **Suite/lane fit:** should arguably be integration lane (uses server + timing), but currently guarded/fast; monitor for flake. **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_login_method_override.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** `--method=mobile` writes `HAPPIER_AUTH_METHOD="mobile"` into `--print --json` cmd; invalid `--method` error includes expected aliases (`web`/`browser`/`mobile`). **Real behavior vs mocks:** subprocess via `auth_testkit`; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium (pins error message text/aliases and `cmd` string fragment). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium. **Duplication candidates:** shares `--print --json` + JSON parse pattern with other auth tests. **Suite/lane fit:** CLI contract test. **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_login_print_includes_configure_links.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** `--print --json` includes computed URLs (`internalServerUrl`, `publicServerUrl`, `webappUrl`), exports `HAPPIER_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL`, and emits `configureServer` deep links (web + mobile). Also validates webapp precedence (`--webapp-url` override, `--webapp=public` override, and stack-env vs global env behavior). **Real behavior vs mocks:** subprocess via `auth_testkit`; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** high (pins exact URL templates + JSON shape). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium. **Duplication candidates:** precedence-matrix style repeats across other flag precedence tests; could be generalized as table-driven `assertAuthPrintJson({ env, args, expect })`. **Suite/lane fit:** CLI contract test. **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_login_respects_pinned_stack_port.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** per-stack auth login port resolution: prefers pinned `HAPPIER_STACK_SERVER_PORT` over stale `stack.runtime.json` port; falls back to runtime port when stack env omits port (ephemeral model); `hstack stack dev <stack> --json` reuses recorded runtime port. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real temp FS storage layout + subprocess (`spawn`) invoking `apps/stack/bin/hstack.mjs`; no internal mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium (pins storage file names/paths + JSON output fields). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium (subprocess + net server used only for ephemeral port selection; potential platform differences). **Duplication candidates:** local `runNode` capture wrapper + “minimal monorepo” scaffolding duplicates other tests; consolidate into a shared stack-storage testkit. **Suite/lane fit:** integration-ish (CLI + filesystem state), but hermetic. **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_login_runtime_state_port.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** when `HAPPIER_STACK_SERVER_PORT` is absent, `hstack auth login --print --json` uses `stack.runtime.json` `ports.server` to compute internal/public URLs and preserves `stackName`. **Real behavior vs mocks:** real temp FS via `auth_testkit` fixture + subprocess; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium (pins runtime JSON schema keys and URL formatting). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium. **Duplication candidates:** overlaps with `auth_login_respects_pinned_stack_port.test.mjs` on runtime port precedence; consider merging into one matrix file. **Suite/lane fit:** integration-ish CLI contract. **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/bundleWorkspaceDeps.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** stack packaging bundler correctness: `bundledDependencies` must be declared in `dependencies`; `bundleWorkspaceDeps()` copies `dist/` + sanitizes `package.json` (removes install scripts, marks private); bundles internal dependency closure (cli-common → agents → protocol) and vendors external dependency trees; validates failure modes (missing dist, malformed JSON). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real filesystem fixtures in temp dir; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** medium–high (pins workspace package layout and sanitizer behavior; can drift with bundler changes). **Speed/flakiness risks:** low–medium (lots of FS IO; no network). **Duplication candidates:** bundling behavior parallels `apps/cli/scripts/bundleWorkspaceDeps.mjs`; ensure shared implementation stays in one place and keep tests aligned. **Suite/lane fit:** build/packaging infra test (appropriate for unit lane if kept fast). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/ci.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** Docker host env resolution prefers per-user Docker Desktop socket path and still works when `HOME` is unset (falls back to CWD). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real filesystem temp dirs; mutates `process.env.HOME` and `process.chdir` (global). **Brittleness risks:** medium (assumes unix socket path semantics; platform-specific). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium (global env/cwd mutation is risky if node:test parallelizes files; ensure isolation/restore remains correct). **Duplication candidates:** env/cwd save-restore logic repeated across files; could be a shared `withTempHomeDir()` helper. **Suite/lane fit:** unit-ish env/path resolver test (appropriate, but be cautious about global mutation). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** (scripts/*.test.mjs, not excluded).

## Integration — apps/stack (node:test)

- **Runner:** node:test
- **Commands:** `yarn --cwd apps/stack test:integration`, `yarn test:integration`
- **Config files:** `apps/stack/scripts/test_integration.mjs`
- **Includes:** `scripts/tests/**/*.(integration|real.integration).test.mjs`
- **Known env vars:** `CI`
- **CI entrypoints (grep):**
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:755:          timeout --signal=KILL --kill-after=30s 25m node --test apps/stack/scripts/self_host_binary_smoke.integration.test.mjs`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:756:          timeout --signal=KILL --kill-after=30s 45m node --test apps/stack/scripts/release_binary_smoke.integration.test.mjs`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:793:          node --test apps/stack/scripts/self_host_systemd.real.integration.test.mjs`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:830:          node --test apps/stack/scripts/self_host_launchd.real.integration.test.mjs`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:865:        run: node --test apps/stack/scripts/self_host_schtasks.real.integration.test.mjs`
  - `.github/workflows/tests.yml:904:        run: node --test apps/stack/scripts/self_host_daemon.real.integration.test.mjs`

- [x] Enumerate shared fixtures/helpers/testkits used (dedupe candidates) — **Shared harnesses/imports across the integration suite:** `apps/stack/scripts/testkit/{auth_testkit,monorepo_port_testkit,stack_script_command_testkit,stack_archive_command_testkit,stack_stop_sweeps_testkit}.mjs`, plus orchestration entrypoints under test (`apps/stack/scripts/{daemon,pm}.mjs`) and shared helpers (`apps/stack/scripts/utils/{auth/{credentials_paths,stable_scope_id}.mjs,pglite_lock.mjs,proc/proc.mjs,stack/stop.mjs,tui/cleanup.mjs}`). **Dedupe hotspot:** the “run script and capture stdout/stderr + env scaffolding” pattern repeats heavily—prefer routing everything through `stack_script_command_testkit.mjs` (or a single unified harness) instead of one-off spawn wrappers.
- [x] Spot-check for internal mocks (disallowed) vs boundary mocks (allowed) — Predominant pattern is **boundary** stubbing (fake binaries via PATH, env gates like `HAPPIER_NO_BROWSER_OPEN`, and hermetic filesystem temp dirs) while running real stack scripts via `node --test`. A few tests implement “fake CLI tool” shims to avoid OS/network/service side effects; those are acceptable boundary mocks, but any module-level mocking of stack domain logic would violate the no-internal-mocks policy (none observed in the initial reviewed subset).
- [x] Identify brittle assertions (copy/snapshots/time/ordering/impl details) — High brittleness surfaces: (1) pinning stdout/stderr help/copy and exact error prefixes, (2) table-driven port/allocation outputs that depend on ordering, and (3) time-based assertions around daemon start verification + lock contention (`pglite_lock`). Prefer asserting stable JSON shapes/error codes/exit statuses where possible, and avoid hardcoding full human text unless it’s a published CLI contract.
- [x] Identify slow/flaky tests and root causes (timeouts, orchestration, parallelism) — Likely hotspots: daemon + service orchestration tests (process groups, detached children, cleanup), port allocation/Metro/Tailscale probes, and any test that depends on filesystem locks (`pglite_lock`) or OS-level service managers (all `.real.integration.test.mjs`). Root causes are mostly external timing + parallelism; `test_integration.mjs` correctly serializes real tests, but regular integration tests can still contend on shared ports/fs unless each test isolates runtime dirs and env.
- [x] Identify duplication/over-testing and consolidation opportunities — Major duplication clusters: (1) monorepo port reservation/apply/validation/conflicts tests (similar fixture graphs + assertions), (2) multiple stop/sweep variants with overlapping env scaffolds, and (3) repeated “spawn stack script + capture + parse JSON” wrappers. Consolidation candidates: a single “stack integration harness” that creates isolated stack home/storage/workspace dirs + helpers for running scripts with consistent timeout/cleanup semantics.
- [x] Confirm CI wiring runs this suite at the right times (PR, release, nightly) — **Confirmed wired:** `apps/stack/package.json` defines `test:integration` as `node ./scripts/test_integration.mjs`, and CI runs `yarn --cwd apps/stack test:integration` in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (PR) and `.github/workflows/release-npm.yml` (release). Additionally, some long-running smoke/real-integration files are invoked directly with explicit `timeout`/serial settings in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (binary smoke + service-manager real tests).

### Test files

- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_copy_from_pglite_lock_in_use.integration.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** `hstack stack auth copy-from <source>` behavior when the source stack’s pglite lock file is held by a *live* PID: expects the flow to **skip DB seeding** and emit “db seed skipped” + “pglite db dir is in use by pid …” guidance, while still exiting 0. **Real behavior vs mocks:** runs the real `scripts/auth.mjs` via `auth_testkit.runNodeCapture`; uses a real long-lived Node process as the lock holder; **boundary stub** for `yarn` via PATH-shim to keep migrations deterministic/fast. **Brittleness risks:** high (asserts on human-readable output substrings; lock file schema + message wording; relies on POSIX PATH `:` behavior). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium (spawns a live PID, timeouts in `terminateChildProcess`, filesystem cleanup). **Duplication candidates:** repeats stack env + temp home/storage/workspace scaffolding used in other auth integration tests; factor into a shared `auth_copy_from_fixture()` helper in `auth_testkit.mjs`. **Suite/lane fit:** integration (correct; exercises cross-file orchestration + lock contention). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `apps/stack/scripts/test_integration.mjs` includeSuffix discovery.
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_copy_from_runCapture.integration.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** regression/contract matrix for `hstack stack auth copy-from`: (1) no `ReferenceError: runCapture is not defined` and migrations resolve `yarn`, (2) prefers source **server-scoped** credential over unrelated legacy `access.key`, (3) prefers source **stable-scope** credential when source stack has no pinned port (even if `HAPPIER_STACK_DISABLE_STABLE_SCOPE=1` leaked), (4) fails closed when legacy token `sub` is missing from source Account rows (offline), (5) accepts source auth when a running source server validates the token, (6) fails closed when source stack isn’t running unless `--offline-ok`, (7) `--no-secret` does not overwrite target master secret (even with `--force`). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real auth script execution + real on-disk credential layouts (`resolveStackCredentialPaths`, stable-scope id derivation) + real temp filesystem; **boundary stubs**: PATH-shim `yarn` and a local HTTP stub server for `/v1/account/profile` + runtime JSON (`stack.runtime.json`) to simulate “source running”. **Brittleness risks:** very high (pins many path/layout conventions, stable-scope ID format, migration command strings like `migrate:sqlite:deploy`, and some error/copy output); large surface makes small policy tweaks expensive. **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium–high (multiple subprocess runs; HTTP server lifecycle; file IO; could flake on slow CI). **Duplication candidates:** heavy duplication of env/stack fixture setup across tests inside the file; consolidate into shared builders in `auth_testkit.mjs` + table-drive cases. **Suite/lane fit:** integration (correct; crosses CLI/home/storage/runtime boundaries). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `apps/stack/scripts/test_integration.mjs` includeSuffix discovery.
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/auth_status_server_validation.integration.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** `hstack stack auth status --json` server-validation contract: when `/v1/account/profile` returns 401 with `{code}`, JSON output marks `auth.serverValidation.checked=true`, `valid=false`, and preserves `status` + `code`; when profile returns 200, output marks `valid=true`, `code='ok'`. **Real behavior vs mocks:** runs real auth script and parses real JSON stdout; uses a local HTTP stub server as a boundary mock for `/health` + `/v1/account/profile` token checks. **Brittleness risks:** medium–high (pins JSON schema fields + exact routing paths and auth header semantics). **Speed/flakiness risks:** low–medium (local server + subprocess). **Duplication candidates:** HTTP stub server patterns overlap other auth integration tests; extract `withStubServer({ routes })` helper in `auth_testkit.mjs`. **Suite/lane fit:** integration (appropriate: script + network boundary). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `apps/stack/scripts/test_integration.mjs` includeSuffix discovery.
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/daemon_invalid_auth_reseed_stack_name.integration.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** daemon invalid-auth auto-reseed behavior in `startLocalDaemonWithAuth(...)`: (1) uses the resolved stack name (no `null` placeholder dirs) when reseeding, (2) overwrites stale target creds with seed creds, (3) fails closed and **does not fall back to `main`** when configured seed creds are stale/invalid, (4) does not overwrite manually-authenticated creds that differ from seed. **Real behavior vs mocks:** exercises real `scripts/daemon.mjs` start/stop logic with real filesystem stack envs + credential files; uses a local HTTP stub server for `/v1/account/profile` (boundary); uses PATH-shim `yarn` and writes a **fake `apps/cli/dist/index.mjs`** to boundary-mock the external `happier daemon` CLI (controls exit codes + log output + daemon.state.json writes). **Brittleness risks:** very high (string-matching fatal log lines, token parsing, and implicit contracts about where daemon writes logs/state; also asserts on absence/presence of specific directories like `<storage>/null`). **Speed/flakiness risks:** medium–high (multiple temp repos/dirs, subprocesses, detached dummy daemons, timing sensitivity around process kill/cleanup). **Duplication candidates:** repeated inline fake CLI scripts across tests; extract a reusable “fake happier daemon CLI” builder that can parameterize attempt sequences and auth outcomes. **Suite/lane fit:** integration (correct: cross-process orchestration + failure recovery semantics). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `apps/stack/scripts/test_integration.mjs` includeSuffix discovery.
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/daemon_start_verification.integration.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** daemon start verification + UX streaming contracts: (1) treat `happier daemon start` exit=0 as failure if daemon never becomes running, (2) stream daemon start output with `[daemon]` prefix when `HAPPIER_STACK_TUI=1`, (3) surface “already running” state in TUI mode when daemon.state.json points at a matching live process, (4) `checkDaemonState()` fallback behavior when `HAPPIER_ACTIVE_SERVER_ID` differs (find any running daemon state for the requested server URL). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real `startLocalDaemonWithAuth`/`checkDaemonState` logic from `scripts/daemon.mjs`; boundary-mocks the external CLI by writing a fake `apps/cli/dist/index.mjs`; uses real detached dummy Node processes to simulate a running daemon; uses runner scripts to capture stdout/stderr from a separate node process. **Brittleness risks:** high (depends on specific log prefix formatting, stable server-id directory names like `stack_dev__id_default`, and process-list/env matching heuristics). **Speed/flakiness risks:** high (detached processes + polling/timeouts + PID/group kill; sensitive on loaded CI). **Duplication candidates:** repeated fake CLI + runner script setup overlaps other daemon integration tests; centralize in a `daemon_testkit` with helpers for “fake daemon start sequence” + “write daemon.state.json + dummy process”. **Suite/lane fit:** integration (appropriate; validates orchestration + UX output). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `apps/stack/scripts/test_integration.mjs` includeSuffix discovery.
- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/exit_cleanup_kills_detached_children_on_crash.integration.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** `installExitCleanup({ children })` behavior on crash: when a parent process throws `uncaughtException`, the registered detached child process group is killed (pid stops being alive within timeout). **Real behavior vs mocks:** real `spawnProc` + `installExitCleanup` from `scripts/utils/proc/*` executed in a spawned “parent” script; no mocks. **Brittleness risks:** very high (POSIX-only semantics; timing windows; PID reuse; assumes `kill(-pid)` process-group behavior). **Speed/flakiness risks:** high (polling + 5s timeout; can flake on busy systems). **Duplication candidates:** overlaps other “detached child + kill-tree” tests in stack and in `packages/tests` process harnesses; consolidate on one canonical proc testkit + shared wait/kill helpers. **Suite/lane fit:** integration (correct; process-group behavior is orchestration-heavy and should not be in unit lane). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `apps/stack/scripts/test_integration.mjs` includeSuffix discovery.

- [x] `apps/stack/scripts/monorepo_port.apply.integration.test.mjs` — **What it covers:** large behavior matrix for `hstack monorepo port`: applies split-repo commits into monorepo subdirs, supports `--skip-applied`, accepts monorepo sources without double-prefixing, supports cloning/autocloning targets, accepts `file://` source URLs, supports `--continue-on-failure` with JSON + non-JSON summaries, auto-skips “identical new file” patches, `--onto-current` semantics, end-to-end CLI registry via `bin/hstack.mjs`, and multi-repo porting into one branch (including renames). **Real behavior vs mocks:** heavy real git repos/commits/branches in temp dirs (via `monorepo_port_testkit.mjs`), real `monorepo.mjs` invocation via Node, and real JSON parsing; no internal mocks. **Brittleness risks:** very high (many git semantics + stdout/JSON surface; long table makes small behavior tweaks expensive; relies on deterministic git env + commit messages). **Speed/flakiness risks:** high (many git operations, multiple subprocess runs, guide path uses TTY simulation + timeouts). **Duplication candidates:** overlaps `monorepo_port.{conflicts,validation}.integration.test.mjs` and repeats monorepo scaffolding patterns; consolidate into fewer high-signal table-driven cases and reuse a single harness for “run port and assert result”. **Suite/lane fit:** integration (correct; core behavior is orchestration + git). **Wiring status:** **confirmed executed** by `apps/stack/scripts/test_integration.mjs` includeSuffix discovery.

## Unit/Integration — packages/relay-server (node:test)

- **Runner:** node:test
- **Commands:** `yarn --cwd packages/relay-server test`, `yarn test:unit`
- **Config files:** `packages/relay-server/package.json`
- **Includes:** `node --test` default discovery (no explicit file args): runs `packages/relay-server/**/**.test.{js,cjs,mjs}` (excludes `node_modules`); currently `scripts/*.test.mjs` + `src/*.test.mjs`
- **Known env vars:** `HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV`, `HAPPIER_CACHE_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `HAPPIER_SERVER_UI_DIR`

### Suite audit TODO

- [x] Confirm lane intent + boundaries (unit vs integration vs e2e) — Fast unit/infra suite for `@happier-dev/relay-server`: mapping/parsing/asset-selection + crypto verification + packaging vendoring contracts. No real GitHub/network orchestration; belongs in unit lane.
- [x] Confirm discovery globs match intent (no accidental includes/excludes) — `packages/relay-server/package.json` runs `node --test` with no file list; default discovery currently picks up exactly 6 files (`src/*.test.mjs`, `scripts/*.test.mjs`). Risk: any future `**/*.test.*` added under this package (outside `node_modules`) will auto-run; intentional but worth noting.
- [x] Enumerate env vars used in this suite (both configs + tests) — Config/script: `HAPPIER_FEATURE_POLICY_ENV` (forced empty in `test` script).
